cause: Verification escapes the working tree: when the agent or a helper it delegates to is unsure, it fetches or searches outside the workspace (remote sources, machine-wide hunts for other copies of the code, pristine copies unpacked elsewhere) to gain confidence instead of re-reading its own diff and re-running the repro. The boundary exists only as prose — helper briefs usually omit it and no one sweeps a helper's actual command log before trusting its verdict — so the escape goes unnoticed and voids the attempt even when the fix is correct.
rule: Resolve uncertainty only from inside the working tree: when a local result confuses you, re-read your diff and re-run the repro rather than fetching or searching outside it; put that ban verbatim in every helper brief, and before trusting any helper's verdict sweep the commands it actually ran for out-of-tree verification (fetches, machine-wide searches, other copies), discarding and redoing in-tree anything found.
predicted_effect: Attempts that would have been voided by an out-of-tree comparison stay in-tree — confusion no longer triggers machine-wide searches or fetched references, and helper reviews no longer smuggle in external evidence — so their often already-correct fixes get scored as passes instead of being thrown away.
learned: Fixes were being thrown away not because they were wrong but because verification slipped outside the working tree — through helpers and self-doubt alike — so the boundary must live verbatim in every helper brief and be swept out of the commands a helper actually ran before its verdict is trusted.
